scope: PR #174 PR-A: the finish-check engine - always-on/finish-check.mjs (the Stop/SubagentStop engine), finish-check-records.md (the record contract), test/finish-check.test.mjs (discriminating tests), ADR-0100, 21 BDD scenarios across the two always-on feature files + features/steps/finish-check.steps.mjs, the 7-line dispatcher edit in edit-gate-select-load.steps.mjs, bdd-config.json (subagent audience), CHANGELOG, coverage-log. The reviewer drove the REAL engine with crafted records/payloads, confirmed the grep-test is clean (only a 'session_id' comment, Stop-payload data not a web session), data ownership and boundary placement are sound (changed files derived once and both the receipt and the review matrix checked against that set; delegation to task-receipt.mjs for grounding), and the fail-closed paths for payload/record/exception/stdin and the spawn-null receipt path are real. It raised three findings (1 high, 1 medium, 1 low), all fixed before this entry.

boundary.evidence: the engine validates record shape and delegates grounding to task-receipt.mjs (the single owner of 'grounded'); no validation leak and no duplication of edit-gate logic (edit-gate is a PreToolUse hook and needs no transcript walk).

ownership.evidence: the changed-file set is derived once from the transcript (the owner); the receipt's changed_files and the review matrix keys are both checked against that derived set, not trusted independently. The block counter has a single owner (the ESK_BLOCKS file via readBlocks/bumpBlocks); escalate does not bump it.

dependency.evidence: grep-test clean: the only match is 'session_id' in a comment (Stop-payload data). Node built-ins plus a spawn of the sibling task-receipt.mjs; no web concerns.

error-handling.evidence: F2 fix: a transcript named in the payload that cannot be read (missing, not a file, open/stat error) now THROWS -> the outer handler blocks (exit 2), distinct from an empty-but-readable transcript (read-only). Payload/record/uncaughtException/stdin all route to block; checkReceipt treats spawn status!==0 (incl null on ENOENT/signal) as a block. The one remaining fail-open corner (readable transcript in an unrecognized schema) is disclosed in ADR-0100 and finish-check-records.md and is PR-B's self-test/canary target.

boundary.evidence: unit tests that spawn the real engine with crafted records/payloads (the lowest level that catches the bug).

error-handling.evidence: F1 fix: added 5 discriminating tests for the previously-unguarded block branches (out-of-order steps, ledger:false, logged:false, a checker missing output_sha256, a matrix row present-but-missing one question) plus 1 for the F2 fail-closed transcript, so a surgical no-op of any of those branches now flips a test. 23 unit tests pass; a no-op engine (always exit 0) flips every block case.

boundary.evidence: 21 scenarios (one @audience:subagent) under new Step 4-9 rules drive the real engine on the harness; the dispatcher edit routes 'the finish check runs' to world.runFinishCheck for #174 and falls back to #175's runFinish, no collision.

ownership.evidence: the record format has one home (finish-check-records.md); the datastore is regenerated from the feature files.

error-handling.evidence: negative scenarios hold at exit 2; happy scenarios assert status 0 (some Thens individually vacuous, acceptable because the negatives + unit tests discriminate). ADR-0100 and records.md disclose the evidence limits and the one remaining fail-open corner.

findings.where: finish-check.mjs block branches vs test/finish-check.test.mjs + the BDD steps
findings.finding: CONFIRMED by driving the real engine: five block branches were LIVE but had no discriminating test (checkOrder out-of-order loop, checkProve ledger, checkProve malformed-checker, checkReview per-question verdict/source, checkReview logged); a surgical no-op of any one kept the whole suite green - the exact false-green the repo's flagship verifiable-quality-gates rule forbids, in the enforcement floor itself.
findings.resolution: fixed: added one discriminating unit test per branch (out-of-order permutation -> /out of order/, ledger:false -> /evidence ledger/, logged:false -> /review log/, checker missing output_sha256 -> /fully recorded/, partial matrix row -> /verdict+source for "error-handling"/). A no-op of each branch now flips its test.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED: a transcript_path pointing at a missing file, a directory, or an unreadable file returned [] -> reclassified as 'read-only' -> exit 0, skipping the entire formula with no operator signal. This is an undisclosed fail-open on an error path, contradicting the ADR's own central property that an unhandled path must land on exit 2.
findings.resolution: fixed: a transcript named in the payload that cannot be read now throws, so the outer handler blocks (fail closed); only an empty-but-readable transcript reads as read-only. A discriminating test (missing transcript -> exit 2) pins it, and the corner is disclosed in ADR-0100 + finish-check-records.md.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED dead code: `priorBlocks >= blockCap || payload.stop_hook_active === true && priorBlocks >= blockCap` - && binds tighter than ||, so the right operand is a strict subset of the left and can never change the outcome; stop_hook_active was effectively ignored despite the comment claiming otherwise.
findings.resolution: fixed: reduced to `priorBlocks >= blockCap` and rewrote the comment to state that stop_hook_active does not change the decision because the block counter already tracks the run.

minorNotes: checkReceipt fails closed on spawn failure (status null on ENOENT/signal satisfies status!==0); reviewer reasoned this from code rather than executing the ENOENT path.
the schema-unrecognized transcript corner remains fail-open by design and is disclosed; PR-B's install-time self-test and canary are the backstop.
happy BDD scenarios assert status 0 across multiple Then lines (individually vacuous); acceptable because the negative scenarios and the 23 unit tests discriminate.
